[Resource from qmd at qmd://prisma/apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/self-relations.mdx] 1: ---
2: title: Self-relations
3: description: How to define and work with self-relations in Prisma.
4: url: /orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/self-relations
5: metaDescription: How to define and work with self-relations in Prisma.
6: metaTitle: Self-relations
7: ---
8: 
9: A relation field can reference its own model, called a _self-relation_. Self-relations can be 1-1, 1-n, or m-n.
10: 
11: :::note
12: Self-relations always require the `@relation` attribute.
13: :::
14: 
15: ## One-to-one self-relations
16: 
17: ```prisma
18: model User {
19:   id          Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
20:   name        String?
21:   successorId Int?    @unique
22:   successor   User?   @relation("BlogOwnerHistory", fields: [successorId], references: [id])
23:   predecessor User?   @relation("BlogOwnerHistory")
24: }
25: ```
26: 
27: This expresses:
28: 
29: - A user can have zero or one predecessor
30: - A user can have zero or one successor
31: 
32: **Key rules:**
33: 
34: - Both sides must use the same `@relation` name
35: - One side must be fully annotated with `fields` and `references`
36: - The foreign key needs `@unique` for 1-1
37: - Cannot be required on both sides (impossible to create first record)
38: 
39: ## One-to-many self relations
40: 
41: ```prisma
42: model User {
43:   id        Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
44:   name      String?
45:   teacherId Int?
46:   teacher   User?   @relation("TeacherStudents", fields: [teacherId], references: [id])
47:   students  User[]  @relation("TeacherStudents")
48: }
49: ```
50: 
51: This expresses:
52: 
53: - A user has zero or one teacher
54: - A user can have zero or more students
55: 
56: No `@unique` constraint on `teacherId` - multiple students can share the same teacher.
57: 
58: ## Many-to-many self relations
59: 
60: ```prisma
61: model User {
62:   id         Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
63:   name       String?
64:   followedBy User[]  @relation("UserFollows")
65:   following  User[]  @relation("UserFollows")
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: This expresses:
70: 
71: - A user can be followed by zero or more users
72: - A user can follow zero or more users
73: 
74: For relational databases, this is an implicit m-n (Prisma manages the relation table).
75: 
76: **Explicit version** (for storing additional fields):
77: 
78: ```prisma
79: model User {
80:   id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
81:   name       String?
82:   followedBy Follows[] @relation("followedBy")
83:   following  Follows[] @relation("following")
84: }
85: 
86: model Follows {
87:   followedBy   User @relation("followedBy", fields: [followedById], references: [id])
88:   followedById Int
89:   following    User @relation("following", fields: [followingId], references: [id])
90:   followingId  Int
91:   @@id([followingId, followedById])
92: }
93: ```
94: 
95: ## Multiple self-relations on same model
96: 
97: You can combine multiple self-relations:
98: 
99: ```prisma
100: model User {
101:   id         Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
102:   name       String?
103:   teacherId  Int?
104:   teacher    User?   @relation("TeacherStudents", fields: [teacherId], references: [id])
105:   students   User[]  @relation("TeacherStudents")
106:   followedBy User[]  @relation("UserFollows")
107:   following  User[]  @relation("UserFollows")
108: }
109: ```
110:

content.text:
The error is because self-relations need an explicit `@relation` name plus `fields`/`references` on the child side and the opposite list field on the parent side. Fix your model:

```prisma
model ProductCategory {
  id               Int               @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt        DateTime          @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime?         @updatedAt
  products         Product[]
  name             String
  description      String?           @db.Text
  tier             Int               @default(1)
  parentCategoryId Int?
  parentCategory   ProductCategory?  @relation("CategoryHierarchy", fields: [parentCategoryId], references: [id])
  childCategories  ProductCategory[] @relation("CategoryHierarchy")

  @@map("productCategories")
}
```

This is a one-to-many self-relation (infinite depth supported), per `prisma/apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/self-relations.mdx` § "One-to-many self relations" (lines 39–56). The rule: both sides need the same `@relation("name")`, and the side with the foreign key (`parentCategoryId`) supplies `fields`/`references`; the other side becomes the list field (`childCategories`) that was missing in your original attempt.
